Decision Escalation Matrix

Producer-Nation Regulatory Adoption Failure or Delay Escalation Level: Steering Council Approval Process: Steering Council convenes within 5 days of notification; reviews the status of MoU commitments and binding national embedding progress. If fewer than 3 of the top-5 rubber-producing nations (Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam) have committed to binding adoption of the SALB Containment Protocol by the proposed Month 54 (2031-04-12) threshold, Council votes on stop/re-scope decision (supermajority ≥66% rule): proceed with partial producer base, extend adoption timeline by 12-24 months, or pivot to alternative protocol authority model. Written rationale and revised programme roadmap published within 30 days. Rationale: The SALB Containment Protocol is the non-negotiable Phase 1 deliverable and precondition for all scale-up. Fewer than 3 binding producer commitments by Month 54 (2031-04-12) means the Month 36 (2029-10-12) gate's protocol-adoption criterion cannot be met and the entire stage-gate logic collapses. This risk exceeds PMO operational authority (USD 50M threshold); it is a strategic programme continuity decision. Negative Consequences: If producer-nation adoption does not reach 3 of top-5 by Month 54 (2031-04-12), the Year 3 gate cannot be passed in full; funding tranche is withheld or released at minimum 80% (USD 5.6B instead of USD 7.0B). Phase 2 scale-up stalls; breeding trials and alternative-crop pilots lose containment mandate. Estimated cost: USD 1.5-3 billion in deferred and redirected capital; programme credibility and funder confidence erode; risk of SALB spread increases if protocol is not binding.

Breeding-Cultivar Yield-Penalty Exceeds Threshold at Interim Checkpoint Escalation Level: Steering Council (with Technical Advisory Group and Resistance Breeding Oversight Group consultation) Approval Process: At Month 48 (2030-10-12), Breeding Programme Director submits interim cultivar-yield data from all 4 trial sites. If cultivar yield is below 85% of elite clones (yield penalty >15%, the proposed threshold), Breeding Coordinator escalates to Steering Council within 5 days. Council convenes by Month 54 (2031-04-12) to decide: (1) continue conventional polygenic breeding and accept lower yield (potentially missing Year 7 gate), (2) initiate crown-budding fast-track fallback (USD 0.25B, fits unallocated balance, compresses timeline by 2-3 years), or (3) re-scope cultivar targets downward. Decision is made by Steering Council supermajority vote (≥66% rule); documented rationale and revised breeding roadmap published within 30 days. Rationale: The Year 7 gate (Month 84 = 2033-10-12) depends on cultivar yield ≥90% of elite clones. The breeding timeline has zero slack: trials must be planted by Month 12 (2027-10-12) to yield 6-year data by Month 84 (2033-10-12). Detecting yield penalties at Month 48 (2030-10-12) (4-year interim checkpoint) is the last decision point to activate a fallback pathway. This decision involves strategic technology choice (conventional vs. crown-budding) and budget reallocation (USD 0.25B from unallocated balance) that exceeds PMO USD 50M operational threshold. Negative Consequences: If yield penalty >15% is confirmed and no fallback is triggered, Year 7 gate is missed; cultivar-readiness KPI cannot be achieved by Month 84 (2033-10-12), withholding Year 7 tranche (USD 6.5B, or minimum 80% = USD 5.2B). OEM offtake agreements are unsigned; alternative-crop plants cannot be financed. Estimated impact: USD 2-3 billion in sunk breeding and field-trial investment; smallholder adoption stalls (cultivars unavailable); programme loses supply-diversification objective.

Alternative-Rubber Cost or Quality KPI Missed by Month 60 (2031-10-12) Checkpoint Escalation Level: Steering Council Approval Process: At Month 60 (2031-10-12), PMO Alternative Crops Workstream submits feedstock and processing-cost assessment against pre-registered Month 60 (2031-10-12) KPI waypoints: feedstock cost ≤USD 1.20/kg dry matter (Guayule), ≤USD 1.00/kg (dandelion); processing cost ≤USD 2.50/kg; quality variance ≤±10%. If targets are significantly missed, PMO escalates to Steering Council by Month 60 (2031-10-12). Council convenes by Month 66 (2032-04-12) to decide: (1) increase processing-innovation R&D capital and defer wave 1 plant commitment, (2) redirect alternative-crop capital to accelerate resistant-Hevea breeding, or (3) narrow portfolio (e.g., dandelion only, Guayule deferred). Decision made by Council supermajority vote; choice documented and resource reallocation approved within 30 days. Rationale: Alternative-rubber cost competitiveness is critical to Year 12 gate KPI (delivered cost <30% above Hevea benchmark). Pilot processing and tire-qualification trials (Months 12-48 = 2027-10-12 to 2030-10-12) generate cost data by Month 60 (2031-10-12). If cost or quality targets are missed, wave 1 commercial plant capex (USD 1.6B) cannot be committed without loss-absorption risk exceeding programme tolerance. This decision involves capital reallocation (USD 0.5-1.5B from processing plants to R&D or breeding) and portfolio scope that exceeds PMO USD 50M authority. Negative Consequences: If cost targets are missed by 20-30% and no decision is made by Month 60 (2031-10-12), wave 1 plant commitment proceeds at high risk; plants are built but operate below cost targets, generating large operating losses. Estimated impact: USD 0.8-1.2 billion in stranded plant capital by Month 120 (2036-10-12); OEM offtake agreements are not signed (delivery cost exceeds OEM price tolerance); Year 12 gate cost KPI is missed, withholding Year 12 tranche (USD 4.5B, or minimum 80% = USD 3.6B); alternative-rubber pillar becomes a financial liability rather than a supply-chain hedge.

Compliance or Data-Integrity Finding Threatens Gate-Verification Credibility Escalation Level: Compliance & Ethics Committee (primary investigation) with escalation to Steering Council if systemic or high-impact Approval Process: Compliance & Ethics Committee investigates allegation within 30 days of report. If investigation uncovers data manipulation, undisclosed conflict of interest, or benefit-sharing non-compliance affecting a critical gate (breeding cultivar data, surveillance incursion reports, smallholder adoption metrics, cost/quality trial results), Committee issues written finding and recommends remedial action or data correction within 30 days. If finding is systemic (affecting >1 workstream or >10% of gate data), Committee escalates to Steering Council and Independent Auditor within 5 days. Steering Council convenes within 10 days to assess gate-closure integrity and decide: (1) proceed with gate verdict as-is with auditor caveat, (2) delay gate closure for 30-60 days pending correction, or (3) commission independent data re-validation. Decision documented and published within 15 days. Rationale: Gate-passage decisions rest on evidence credibility. The Independent Auditor validates gate evidence but depends on data integrity from the PMO and site-level partners. If Compliance Committee detects significant data issues (corruption, falsification, concealment), the auditor verdict itself becomes questionable and funder confidence erodes. This risk is beyond PMO and Auditor scope; only the Steering Council can authorize a gate re-evaluation or delay. Negative Consequences: If data-integrity findings are not escalated and corrected before a gate verdict, the auditor's gate closure is later challenged by funders or discovered in post-hoc audit. Reputational damage to the programme: estimated 20-30% funder-confidence loss. If a gate verdict is later overturned due to integrity issues, tranches may be recalled or withheld retroactively (estimated USD 1-2 billion exposure). Legal liability and sanctions risk for programme leadership and involved institutions.

Critical Risk Materialization or Unforeseeable External Shock Escalation Level: Steering Council (emergency session within 10 days) Approval Process: PMO risk officer identifies risk materialization (e.g., major geopolitical event, catastrophic climate event, pandemic-scale disruption, unexpected SALB incursion in a currently unaffected region, major funder defection) that threatens programme schedule or budget by >USD 500 million or >12 months. Risk officer escalates to Steering Council chair within 5 days with impact assessment. Steering Council convenes emergency session within 10 days. Council assesses: (1) is contingency reserve (USD 4.5B) sufficient to address shock, or (2) does shock require programme re-scoping or re-sequencing? If reserve deployment >USD 250M is needed, Council authorizes use; if >USD 500M, Council seeks funder consultation within 30 days. Decision and revised mitigation roadmap documented and communicated to all stakeholders within 30 days. Rationale: Risks exceeding defined thresholds (budget >USD 500M impact, timeline >12 months) are beyond PMO operational ability to absorb or mitigate alone. Contingency reserve deployment, funder consultation, and programme re-sequencing are strategic decisions requiring Council authority. External shocks (trade war, climate extreme, pandemic, geopolitical conflict) are inherently unpredictable but must be escalated and managed transparently to maintain funder trust. Negative Consequences: If critical risks are not escalated and managed centrally, they fragment into localized PMO-level workarounds that may be contradictory or deplete operational budgets without Council visibility. Estimated impact: USD 0.5-1.5 billion in uncoordinated spend; loss of funder confidence and potential funding withdrawal; programme timeline slips by 12-24 months; gate passage is jeopardized. Reputational damage if risk response appears reactive or unplanned.

Smallholder-Adoption Uptake Falls Below Waypoint Threshold Escalation Level: Steering Council (with Smallholder Delivery Oversight and PMO consultation) Approval Process: At Month 84 (2033-10-12), PMO Smallholder Delivery Workstream conducts farmer surveys and clean-plant-network enrollment audits. If enrollment in the clean-plant network and extension programme is <30% of eligible smallholders (the proposed waypoint threshold), Smallholder Delivery Coordinator escalates to Steering Council by Month 90 (2034-04-12). Council reviews adoption indicators and decides: (1) increase extension-corps funding and income-bridging-finance availability to boost uptake toward 40-50%, (2) accept lower adoption (30-40%) and adjust Year 12-18 smallholder-area targets downward, reducing resistant-cultivar deployment acreage, or (3) reallocate capital from smallholder to estate-scale Hevea trials. Decision is made by Council supermajority vote; revised adoption strategy and resource allocation documented within 30 days. Rationale: Smallholder adoption is foundational to the programme's equity and supply-chain resilience goals. Planning targets 45% adoption (2.25 million ha by Month 144 = 2038-10-12) but historical uptake in developing-country agricultural programmes averages 20-40%. By Month 84 (2033-10-12), if extension and finance systems are not generating at least 30% enrollment, either systems are broken (requiring remedial investment) or adoption targets are unrealistic (requiring re-scoping). This decision involves capital reallocation (USD 0.3-0.5B between smallholder finance, extension, and alternative crops) that exceeds PMO USD 50M authority. Negative Consequences: If smallholder uptake remains below 30% and no decision is made, by Month 144 (2038-10-12) resistant-cultivar acreage achieves only 0.75-1.2 million ha (vs. 2.25M target). Regional SALB containment cannot be demonstrated; Year 12 gate smallholder-adoption KPI is missed, contributing to a conditional or failed gate verdict. Estimated impact: USD 1.5-2.5 billion in sunk extension and replant-finance investment yields <50% of planned adoption; alternative-crop supply is undersized due to lack of smallholder participation; programme fails to deliver on equity and livelihood-resilience objectives.

Monitoring Progress

1. Stage-Gate KPI Verification and Funding Release Authorization

Monitoring Tools/Platforms:

  • Independent Auditor Gate-Closure Reports (pre-registered methodology, field audits 30-40%, database audits 40-50%, stakeholder interviews 20-30%)
  • Gate Evidence Submission Template (PMO compiles protocol adoption, breeding cultivar data, alternative-rubber cost/quality, smallholder adoption metrics)
  • Pre-Registered KPI Definitions Document (Month 36/84/144/216 = 2029-10-12, 2033-10-12, 2038-10-12, 2044-10-12 gate criteria, pass/fail/conditional thresholds, validated by Technical Advisory Group)
  • Steering Council Gate Decision Minute (authorization to release tranches; minimum 80% rule for partial passes; dispute escalation to Adjudication Panel)

Frequency: Four gates at Months 36, 84, 144, 216 (2029-10-12, 2033-10-12, 2038-10-12, 2044-10-12); PMO submission 6 months before each gate; auditor field verification Months 30-36 (2029-04-12 to 2029-10-12), 78-84, 138-144, 210-216; verdict issued 30 days before gate deadline

Responsible Role: Independent International Auditor (contracted firm, independent of PMO and Steering Council); Technical Advisory Group (6-8 specialists providing scientific input on breeding, phytosanitary, processing interpretation); Gate Adjudication Panel (neutral arbitration if Steering Council disputes auditor verdict)

Adaptation Process: Auditor verdict determines capital tranche release (USD 7.0B/6.5B/4.5B/4.0B at gates). If gate is PASS, full tranche authorized within 45 days. If CONDITIONAL (partial KPI achievement), minimum 80% released (USD 5.6B/5.2B/3.6B/3.2B). If FAIL, Steering Council convenes within 5 days to authorize either adjudication review, remedial action plan, or capital reallocation. PMO adjusts subsequent-phase delivery targets based on gate verdict (e.g., if breeding gate is conditional, reduce small-holder acreage targets; if cost gate fails, redirect to processing R&D or resistant-Hevea allocation).

Adaptation Trigger: Gate-closure verdict as defined in pre-registered KPI framework: Month 36 (2029-10-12) protocol adoption (IPPC vote passed, ≥3 of top-5 producers binding, ≥100 inspectors, ≥95% red-team detection); Month 84 (2033-10-12) cultivar yield ≥90% elite clones, ≥3 resistance sources, lesion <5mm, defoliation <20%; Month 144 (2038-10-12) alternative-rubber delivered cost <30% above Hevea, 16,000 t/year capacity, ≥40% smallholder adoption; Month 216 (2044-10-12) verified containment maintained, diversified supply chains operational, climate resilience demonstrated. Auditor verdict is binding unless Steering Council initiates formal adjudication within 15 days.

2. SALB Containment Protocol Adoption and Compliance Monitoring

Monitoring Tools/Platforms:

  • Bilateral MoU Status Tracker (Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam binding commitment progress, national regulatory embedding timelines)
  • Compliance-Certificate Database and Mobile Lot-Tracking System (100,000+ inspected nursery lots per year, certified chain-of-custody, real-time inspector deployment roster)
  • Red-Team Drill Reports (protocol enforcement effectiveness tests, detection accuracy, response-speed validation, Months 18-36 = 2028-04-12 to 2029-10-12)
  • Quarterly Containment Compliance Dashboard (share of nurseries under inspection, material moved under certified chain-of-custody, violations detected, penalties imposed)
  • Incursion Alert Verification Log (surveillance detections, confirmation timeliness, false-alarm rate, escalation to response playbook)

Frequency: Monthly internal monitoring (Containment Authority compliance manager); quarterly compliance reporting to Steering Council and PMO; annual compliance audits (validator team); red-team drills at least 3 events over Months 18-36 (2028-04-12 to 2029-10-12); real-time alert verification (within 2 weeks of surveillance report)

Responsible Role: SALB Containment Protocol Authority (Compliance & Enforcement Manager, Deputy Director for Compliance Inspection); 100+ trained compliance inspectors deployed across top 5 producers (20 per country minimum); national plant-protection agency partners; Compliance & Ethics Committee (annual independent audit of inspector performance and data quality)

Adaptation Process: Quarterly compliance data is compiled and reviewed by Containment Authority Compliance Manager and escalated to Steering Council. If nursery-inspection coverage drops below 30,000 lots/year (vs. 100,000+ target), trigger inspector recruitment surge or subcontract with certified micro-multiplier networks. If compliance violations exceed 5% of inspected lots, tighten inspection frequency or suspend nursery certifications. If detection latency exceeds 3 months in primary producers or 6 months in secondary regions, escalate to Surveillance Sensing Architecture for detection-method enhancement (add instrumented spore traps, satellite imaging, or lab capacity). Protocol penalty schedule is enforced uniformly (fines 5-10x value of affected material); non-compliance patterns by country trigger diplomatic escalation to Steering Council for bilateral MoU renegotiation. Red-team drill failures (detection accuracy below 95%, response time beyond 2 weeks) trigger protocol enforcement retraining and inspector-network restructuring.

Adaptation Trigger: Non-compliance rate ≥5% at any inspection milestone; detection latency >6 months in primary producers or >12 months in secondary regions; nursery-inspection coverage <30,000 lots/year; fewer than 3 of top-5 producers with binding national embedding by Month 54 (2031-04-12) (stop/re-scope trigger); red-team drill detection accuracy <95%; zero containment-protocol adoption by Month 36 (2029-10-12) (Month 36 = 2029-10-12 gate fail).

Monitoring Tools/Platforms:

  • Pre-Registered Breeding Objectives Document (yield ≥90% of elite clones, ≥3 stacked resistance sources, lesion size <5mm, defoliation <20%, 10x-inoculum durability testing)
  • Technical Advisory Group breeding pathology assessment (pathogen-variant surveillance, resistance-durability signals, cross-site variability analysis)

Frequency: Monthly site-manager reports to Breeding Programme Director; quarterly multi-site data reviews (Months 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72 = 2027-10-12, 2028-10-12, 2029-10-12, 2030-10-12, 2031-10-12, 2032-10-12); annual breeding-progress update to Steering Council; interim yield-penalty checkpoint at Month 48 (2030-10-12); final cultivar selection by Month 72 (2032-10-12); post-release durability monitoring quarterly from Month 84 (2033-10-12) onward

Responsible Role: Breeding Programme Director (hired by Month 3, 2027-01-12); Regional Deputy Directors for Brazil, Thailand/Southeast Asia, Côte d'Ivoire (hired by Month 9, 2027-07-12); Breeding Coordinator (data management, multi-site protocol consistency); Site Managers at 4 breeding locations; Technical Advisory Group pathologist (durability consultant); Compliance & Ethics Committee (annual breeding-data integrity audits)

Adaptation Process: Quarterly data reviews assess yield penalties, resistance stacking progress, and durability signals. If yield penalty exceeds 15% (cultivar yield <85% of elite) at Month 48 (2030-10-12), Breeding Programme Director escalates to Steering Council within 5 days. Council decides by Month 54 (2031-04-12): (1) continue conventional breeding (accepts potential Year 7 gate delay), (2) initiate crown-budding fast-track fallback (USD 0.25B budget, compresses timeline 2-3 years), or (3) re-scope cultivar yield targets downward. If multi-site interpretation is contentious (one site shows poor durability, others show good), escalate to Technical Advisory Group pathologist for independent assessment. If data integrity concerns arise (missing records, inconsistent measurements), escalate to Compliance & Ethics Committee. By Month 60 (2031-10-12), breeding team initiates second-generation cultivar breeding using different resistance sources, ensuring replacements are available by Month 120 (2036-10-12) if first-generation durability breaks down post-release.

Adaptation Trigger: Yield penalty exceeds 15% by Month 48 (2030-10-12) (triggers crown-budding decision); cultivar yield below 90% of elite clones by Month 72 (2032-10-12) (threatens Year 7 gate pass); resistance sources reduce from 3+ to <3 confirmed independent sources; lesion size >5mm or defoliation >20% confirmed at 2+ sites; durability breakdown detected during sentinel-planting monitoring (Months 84-144 = 2033-10-12 to 2038-10-12) (triggers next-generation breeding acceleration); data-integrity allegation affecting trial records (escalates to Compliance & Ethics investigation).

Monitoring Tools/Platforms:

  • Portfolio-Decision Framework (gate decision logic: continue, pivot to processing R&D, or redirect to resistant-Hevea breeding)
  • Wave 1 and Wave 2 Plant FID and Financial Model (capex, opex, DSCR, financing structure, based on pilot performance)

Frequency: Monthly pilot-plant operations data (Alternative Crops Workstream); quarterly cost-analysis reviews at Months 36, 48, 60 (2029-10-12, 2030-10-12, 2031-10-12); tire-qualification trial results published as available (target monthly, Months 24-48 = 2028-10-12 to 2030-10-12); semi-annual processing-innovation R&D progress reports; annual alternative-crop update to Steering Council

Responsible Role: PMO Alternative Crops Workstream Coordinator (recruited by Month 6, 2027-04-12); pilot-plant operators (Guayule and dandelion sites); processing engineers; OEM Engagement Lead (coordinate tire-qualification trials and offtake negotiations); Finance Manager (cost-analysis and plant-financing models); Technical Advisory Group processing specialist (assess cost and quality KPI achievement)

Adaptation Process: At Months 36, 48, and 60 (2029-10-12, 2030-10-12, 2031-10-12), Alternative Crops Workstream compiles feedstock yield, extraction efficiency, feedstock cost (Guayule ≤USD 1.20/kg dry matter, dandelion ≤USD 1.00/kg), extraction yield (Guayule ≥85%, dandelion ≥80%), processing cost (target ≤USD 2.50/kg), and quality variance (±10%). If targets are missed by 10-20%, escalate to PMO and note as risk to Year 12 gate. If targets are missed by >20%, escalate to Steering Council by Month 60 (2031-10-12) for portfolio decision: (1) increase processing-innovation R&D capital (fund advanced extraction or separation technology), (2) redirect alternative-crop capital to resistant-Hevea breeding prioritization, or (3) narrow portfolio (e.g., dandelion only, Guayule deferred). Wave 1 commercial-plant FID (USD 1.6B capex for 8 plants) is authorized only after Month 60 (2031-10-12) decision and conditional on pilot and tire-qualification results. Wave 2 FID only after Month 144 (2038-10-12) gate (if PASS or CONDITIONAL). If processing-cost or quality targets are missed by Month 84 (2033-10-12), trigger alternative-crop operating-shortfall funding (draw from USD 0.6B loss-cover line item or contingency reserve).

Adaptation Process: Quarterly smallholder surveys track enrollment and uptake progress. If enrollment is below 25% (conservative scenario), escalate to Steering Council by Month 90 (2034-04-12): increase extension funding and income-support payments to boost uptake, or accept lower adoption (30-40%) and adjust Year 12-18 smallholder-area targets downward, reducing resistant-cultivar deployment acreage. Monthly finance-disbursement tracking identifies loan approval delays (escalate to national agricultural banks) and default/arrears trends (if >15%, trigger remedial support: additional technical assistance, group-guarantee restructuring). If replant-loan default or early abandonment suggests farmers are reverting to old cultivars, escalate to extension team for farmer re-engagement and mid-course correction. Annual fraud audits by Compliance & Ethics Committee flag misused replant finance or false-adoption claims; confirmed cases are investigated and remedial actions (repayment demands, exclusion from future finance) are enforced.

Adaptation Process: Whistleblower reports are investigated within 30 days. If investigation uncovers data manipulation or conflict of interest affecting a critical gate (e.g., cultivar yield data, surveillance reports, smallholder metrics, cost/quality trial data), Compliance & Ethics Committee escalates to the Independent Auditor within 5 days. Auditor assesses impact on gate-closure integrity and reports to Steering Council. If systemic corruption or significant data errors are found before a gate verdict, Steering Council authorizes gate delay (30-60 days) for data re-validation or correction. Benefit-sharing audits verify that royalty calculations match ABS agreements and that community payments are disbursed on schedule (annual, linked to cultivar deployment); if payments are delayed or miscalculated, ABS Specialist executes corrective payments within 30 days and reports findings to Steering Council. Breeding-data integrity audits verify trial protocols compliance, measurement consistency across sites, and resistance-gene validation accuracy; if errors are detected, independent validators flag impact on KPI assessments for auditor consideration. Smallholder-finance fraud audits identify loan document falsification, income-support payment fraud, or misuse; confirmed fraud is reported to national authorities and remediated through loan recall or exclusion from future finance.

Adaptation Trigger: Whistleblower report of corruption, conflict of interest, or data manipulation (escalates to investigation within 24 hours); investigation finding of systemic issue affecting >1 workstream (escalates to Steering Council for response authorization); benefit-sharing payment delay >30 days (escalates to Steering Council and funders); breeding-data anomaly detected (unexplained data variance at one site, measurement inconsistency across sites, missing records) (escalates to auditor); smallholder-finance fraud detected (loan document falsification, income-support payment embezzlement) (escalates to law enforcement and programme remediation); Code of Conduct compliance attestation failure >5% of personnel (triggers retraining and policy reinforcement).
